triggerCases.prompt: Before I run a GitHub Enterprise CLI command against https://github.example.com, how should I verify the approved access route? Do not configure credentials, proxies, or environment variables.
Summarize this GitHub Enterprise CLI access guidance in three short paragraphs for a nontechnical reader. Do not inspect a repository, run commands, or configure anything.
Use the GitHub pull request title and description to improve this session title, then keep it anchored when I ask for a supporting follow-up issue.

outputCases.prompt: Using the supplied context, determine the safe next step before running a GitHub Enterprise CLI command. Do not configure credentials, proxies, or environment variables.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: A read-only GitHub Enterprise access preflight that derives the target host from the supplied URL, verifies an approved route before relying on it, and does not invent local proxy configuration.
assertions: The preflight derives the target Enterprise host from the supplied URL instead of assuming GitHub.com.
The response verifies an approved access route with a harmless request before depending on Enterprise CLI access.
If Enterprise access is unavailable, the response follows an offered retry configuration or asks the user to establish an approved route rather than inventing proxy, host, or credential settings.
The response remains read-only and does not edit source, commit, push, or modify a pull request.

outputCases.prompt: Using the supplied context, choose the task title after the follow-up issue is opened. Return only the title.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: The title uses a concise subject that accurately reflects the pull request and remains anchored to the primary pull-request review after the supporting issue is opened.
assertions: The subject accurately reflects that `ThemeProvider` omits color properties when neither provided nor inherited; exact wording and punctuation can differ from the source title.
The subject is concise and uses the pull-request metadata instead of a generic label such as `Review Gutenberg PR`.
The supporting follow-up issue does not replace the primary pull-request reference or subject.
The response contains only the title.

outputCases.prompt: Using the supplied context, choose the task title when canonical GitHub metadata is unavailable. Return only the title.
outputCases.expectedOutcome: The title uses the verified context supplied by the user without inventing unavailable GitHub metadata.
assertions: The subject accurately reflects the user-supplied expired-session redirect loop; exact wording and punctuation can differ from the supplied title.
The title does not invent issue details that are absent from the supplied context.
The response contains only the title.
